name: Delhi–Amritsar–Katra Expressway

route.start: Jasaur Kheri (KMP Expressway), Jhajjar district, Haryana

timeline.event: Prime Minister lays the foundation stone on 5 January and construction gets under way
The roughly 135 km Haryana stretch, from the KMP Expressway to the Punjab border near Kaithal, opens to traffic
Prime Minister formally inaugurates the first phase on 17 July — the already-open Haryana stretch plus a newly built 31 km section near Jalandhar

history: This expressway is being built so that people can drive from Delhi to Amritsar in about four hours and to Katra — the base town for the Vaishno Devi shrine — in about six, instead of the eleven or twelve hours the old NH 44 route takes. It starts from the KMP Expressway near Delhi and runs as a brand-new road across Haryana and Punjab, deliberately skirting the big cities so it never gets tangled in their traffic. A separate branch of about 99 km leaves the main road near Nakodar and heads to Amritsar, passing several important Sikh pilgrimage towns including Sultanpur Lodhi, Goindwal Sahib, Khadoor Sahib and Tarn Taran. The Haryana part opened in 2024 and a Jalandhar-area stretch followed in July 2026, while much of the Punjab and Jammu section is still being built. Officials have targeted 2027 for the whole route.
facts: Planned total length is about 669 km, making it one of India's longest expressway projects.
A roughly 99 km branch leaves the main road near Nakodar and heads to Amritsar.
The 135 km Haryana stretch opened to traffic in 2024.
Being built by NHAI under the Bharatmala programme.
Will end at Katra, the gateway town to the Vaishno Devi shrine.
The Amritsar branch links four major Sikh pilgrimage towns on one road.
Should cut Delhi–Katra driving time from about 12 hours to roughly 6.
Carries the national expressway number NE-5, with the Amritsar branch as NE-5A.
significance: This is India's big pilgrimage highway. Vaishno Devi near Katra draws crores of visitors a year, the Golden Temple at Amritsar draws crores more, and the Amritsar branch strings together several of Sikhism's most visited shrines — all on one fast road from the capital. It also matters for defence and trade: it is a second, faster route toward Jammu and the border areas, taking pressure off NH 44.

travelNotes: Only parts of the route are open, so a Delhi–Katra trip today still means joining and leaving the old NH 44 in places — check which sections are running before you plan. The finished Haryana stretch is fast and very empty, but it runs through open farmland with few fuel pumps and food stops so far, so fill up before you get on. Pilgrim traffic peaks sharply around Navratri and the summer holidays, and winter fog can be thick across Haryana and Punjab in December and January.
futureUpgrades: The full Delhi–Amritsar–Katra route is targeted for completion by 2027.
The Jammu & Kashmir packages between Hiranagar, Samba and Jammu are in the final stages of construction.
